 ORDER

Present miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act is filed against the award dated 28.10.2015 passed by fifth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena in Claim Case No.134/2015.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts in brief to decide this appeal in brief are that the appellant - claimant filed a claim petition under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act for grant of compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in a motor accident occurred on 14.09.2012 involving motorcycle bearing registration No. MP06 MA 9725.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No. 1 - driver/owner of the offending vehicle filed his written statements and opposed the averments made in the claim petition.
It was further stated that since the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No. 3 - insurance company, therefore, insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

Respondent No. 2 - Insurance Company of the offending vehicle also filed its written statement and denied the allegations made in the claim petition stating therein that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the policy terms and conditions, therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

Learned counsel for the appellant argued that learned Claims Tribunal has erred in dismissing the claim petition ignoring the fact that the claimant has mentioned the right vehicle number in his statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. Learned Claims Tribunal has also not considered that oral testimony of the witness of the claimant while dismissing the petition.
Further submission is that learned Claims Tribunal has also erred in calculating the compensation amount on lower side, therefore, instant appeal be allowed and impugned award be dismissed.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has argued that in view of the evidence available on record, learned Claims Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition, therefore, present appeal deserves to be dismissed having no merits.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

As per the fact pleaded in the claim petition as well as the statement of the claimant - Halukanath,
the accident occurred on 14.09.2012 at about 5 pm when he along with Jagdish Rawat was travelling on motorcycle bearing registration No. MP06/MA/9725.

Claimant-witness No. 2 - Vijay Singh also narrated the same story in his examination in chief and stated that the accident has occurred on account of rash and negligent driving by Jagdish who was riding on the motorcycle bearing registration No.MP06/MA/9725.
Claimant - Halukanath in his statement mentioned that he got the FIR (Ex.P/2) registered on the same day i.e. on 14.09.2012.

Perusal of the FIR reveals that the FIR was registered by the claimant-Halukanath himself and as per his version in FIR, the accident occurred by rash and negligent driving of the driver of vehicle bearing registration No. MP/06/HB/6092 not by the vehicle bearing registration No.MP06/MA/9725 as mentioned by him and his witness- Vijay Singh(AW/2).

Learned counsel for the appellant argued that claimant was not a writer of the FIR and mere mention of wrong vehicle number does not affect the merits of the case, however, the above argument is not acceptable because FIR was signed by the claimant and also read over to him.
If in the FIR wrong vehicle number was mentioned he could have objected the same.
However, there is no evidence on record to show that the claimant has ever raised any objection before the police authority for wrong mention of the vehicle number in FIR.
The record also reveals that FIR has been registered after a delay of one month i.e. 13.10.2012 for which no explanation has been given.
There is contradiction in FIR as well as statement of the complainant in respect to alleged vehicle involved in the accident.

No explanation has been given for contradiction of description (motorcycle number Halukanath vs Jagdeesh on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78313377/
2 mentioned in the FIR) and statement of the claimant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In these circumstances, the findings of the learned Claims Tribunal is found to be in accordance with the evidence on record in respect to dismissal of the claim petition.
In this case offending vehicle was not insured with the respondent No. 2/Insurance Company.
The said fact is proved by the evidence of Devendra Prasad Sharma who has been examined by respondent/Insurance Company.
As far as quantam of compensation calculated by the learned Claims Tribunal in view of the evidence adduced by the claimant, learned Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation.
Consequently, the award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal is found to be in accordance with the facts of law, hence, no interference is warranted in the present appeal.
Accordingly, the appeal sans merit and is hereby dismissed.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE (LJ*)
